title: Asia General Knowledge
description: 36 original questions exploring Asian peaks, rivers, Silk Road cities, heritage, and culture (Multiple Choice & Free-Text).
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain above sea level on Earth, located in the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest rises to 8,848.86 meters on the Nepal-Tibet border.

questions.prompt: Which iconic white marble mausoleum stands in Agra, India?
questions.explanation: Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1632.

questions.prompt: Which ancient fortification stretches thousands of kilometers across northern China?
questions.explanation: Built across multiple dynasties, the Great Wall defended China's northern frontier.

questions.prompt: Which sacred snow-capped volcano is Japan's highest mountain?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji stands 3,776 meters tall southwest of Tokyo.

questions.prompt: Which Asian country is the world's largest archipelago state by number of islands (over 17,000)?
questions.explanation: Indonesia spans from Sumatra in the west to New Guinea in the east.

questions.prompt: Which ancient overland network of trade routes linked China with the Mediterranean world?
questions.explanation: The Silk Road carried silk, paper, spices, ideas, and technologies across Eurasia.

questions.prompt: Which country is home to the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur?
questions.explanation: The 452-meter Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.

questions.prompt: Which Asian river is considered sacred in Hinduism and flows across northern India?
questions.explanation: The Ganges flows from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.prompt: What is the longest river in Asia?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze stretches about 6,300 kilometers entirely within China.

questions.prompt: Which traditional Japanese art involves folding paper into decorative shapes?
questions.explanation: Origami comes from 'ori' (folding) and 'kami' (paper).

questions.prompt: Which vast cold desert spans parts of northern China and southern Mongolia?
questions.explanation: The Gobi is a rain-shadow desert north of the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.prompt: Which Asian nation is nicknamed the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
questions.explanation: In Japanese, Nihon / Nippon literally means 'origin of the sun'.

questions.prompt: In which Southeast Asian country is the vast Angkor Wat temple complex located?
questions.explanation: Built in the 12th century, Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world.

questions.prompt: Which city-state sits at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula?
questions.explanation: Singapore became an independent sovereign republic in 1965.

questions.prompt: Which high-altitude plateau in Asia is nicknamed the 'Roof of the World'?
questions.explanation: The Tibetan Plateau averages over 4,500 meters in elevation.

questions.prompt: What is the world's largest landlocked country, located in Central Asia?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan covers over 2.7 million square kilometers.

questions.prompt: Which inland saltwater lake between Asia and Europe is the largest enclosed body of water on Earth?
questions.explanation: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, including Kazakhstan, Iran, and Russia.

questions.prompt: Which major river flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam?
questions.explanation: The Mekong supports tens of millions of people across mainland Southeast Asia.

questions.prompt: Which Korean alphabet was commissioned by King Sejong the Great in the 15th century?
questions.explanation: Hangul was designed so everyday citizens could learn to read and write easily.

questions.prompt: Which mountain on the Pakistan-China border is the second-highest peak in the world?
questions.explanation: K2 rises 8,611 meters in the Karakoram range.

questions.prompt: Which island nation south of India was historically known as Ceylon?
questions.explanation: Ceylon adopted the name Sri Lanka in 1972.

questions.prompt: Which Siberian lake in Russia is the deepest freshwater lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal plunges to 1,642 meters and holds about 20% of Earth's unfrozen fresh water.

questions.prompt: Which historic imperial palace complex sits at the center of Beijing?
questions.explanation: The Forbidden City served as the Chinese imperial palace for nearly 500 years.

questions.prompt: Which strategic waterway between Malaysia and Indonesia is one of the busiest shipping lanes on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Malacca connects the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Silk Road oasis city in Uzbekistan is famed for Registan Square?
questions.explanation: Samarkand flourished as the capital of the Timurid Empire.

questions.prompt: Which Himalayan kingdom measures national progress using 'Gross National Happiness'?
questions.explanation: Bhutan introduced Gross National Happiness in the 1970s.

questions.prompt: Which island shared by Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei is the third-largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Borneo is the only island politically divided among three sovereign nations.

questions.prompt: Which massive 9th-century Buddhist monument on the island of Java is the world's largest Buddhist temple?
questions.explanation: Borobudur features nine stacked platforms topped by a central dome.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Indus Valley civilization city in modern Pakistan was renowned for advanced urban drainage?
questions.explanation: Mohenjo-daro flourished around 2500 BCE with grid streets and covered drains.

questions.prompt: Which river is known as the 'Cradle of Chinese Civilization' for its loess-rich silt?
questions.explanation: The Yellow River (Huang He) is China's second-longest river.

questions.prompt: Which desert in northwestern China's Tarim Basin is one of the largest shifting-sand deserts in the world?
questions.explanation: Silk Road caravans skirted the northern and southern edges of the Taklamakan.

questions.prompt: Which ancient city in Myanmar is famous for a plain containing more than 2,000 Buddhist pagodas and temples?
questions.explanation: Bagan was the capital of the Pagan Kingdom from the 9th to 13th centuries.

questions.prompt: Which mountain pass connects Pakistan and Afghanistan through the Spin Ghar mountains?
questions.explanation: The Khyber Pass has been a crucial trade and strategic corridor for millennia.

questions.prompt: Which Japanese former imperial capital served as the nation's capital for over 1,000 years until 1868?
questions.explanation: Kyoto is renowned for its classical wooden temples, shrines, and gardens.

questions.prompt: Which ocean trench east of the Philippines and Mariana Islands contains Earth's deepest known point?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench reaches nearly 11,000 meters depth.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Persian ceremonial capital was founded by Darius I around 518 BCE in southern Iran?
questions.explanation: Persepolis was the ceremonial heart of the Achaemenid Empire.
